prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: a portrait illustration for the 1985 chapter of a dark Jackie Leven tribute website, part of an existing series.

INPUTS: Image 1 is the ORIGINAL photograph and the authority for Jackie Leven's identity, age, facial proportions, hair and characteristic turned pose with the raised coat collar. Image 2 is only the approved SERIES STYLE reference: emulate its subdued neutral greys, broad ink shapes, dry-brush strokes and edges dissolving into darkness. Do not substitute the younger face or hair from image 2.

SUBJECT AND COMPOSITION: Jackie Leven around 1985, clean-shaven, dark swept-back medium-length hair, serious and slightly guarded expression. Preserve his exact distinctive facial features from image 1: eyes and their heavy lower lids, brows, long nose, mouth and full lower face. No idealization, slimmer face, altered age or generic handsome man. A new waist-up composition in vertical 4:5 format: shoulders and torso angled away, head turned back to look directly at the viewer, as in the photograph. Retain the high turned-up coat collar, which frames his jaw and gives the portrait its character. Show a little more of the coat and shoulder than in the photo, centered within the portrait frame; allow ample dark space above the hair and around the silhouette. No invented hand gesture or accessories.

MEDIUM AND ABSTRACTION: visibly drawn with broad, rough dry-brush ink, restrained directional hatching and large calm grey planes. Moderately abstract in the same manner as image 2. Keep precise but sparse marks for the eyes, nose and mouth; simplify skin modelling to three or four coherent value shapes, not many tiny photographic skin details. Hair becomes a dark silhouette with several broken sweeping strokes. The coat is drawn in muted middle-dark greys and charcoal, with bold incomplete strokes for collar, lapels, shoulder and sleeve. Suggest its original checked fabric only with a handful of broken linear marks, never a regular detailed plaid. Let the lower torso and far shoulder dissolve into the background in irregular dry-brush gaps. This must look hand-drawn, not a photo with a texture filter, digital vector cutout, smooth airbrush, polygon mosaic or glossy oil painting.

BACKGROUND AND PALETTE: near-black anthracite #0d0f12, with only very faint abstract scumbled marks. Do not reproduce the wooden boards, seams or setting in the photograph. Fully neutral black and grey, no brown, sepia, beige, cream, cyan or other colour cast. The pale coat in the source must become subdued neutral grey so it belongs naturally in a dark webpage. Low-key watermark-like presence with readable facial features; highlights should not be white or glaring. Natural positive light/shadow: dark pupils, brows, nostrils and mouth within grey facial planes, never a photographic negative.

OUTPUT: one standalone 4:5 portrait, no panels, typography, logo, signature, frame or watermark lettering.
